title: B4c: bench.match normalizes display names (strip parenthetical suffix, prefer the max variant)
spec:
Why: the first live `orchestrator bench fetch` (2026-09-17 16:17 UTC) parsed 25 model names but matched 0 of 8 hints, because the site's display names carry an effort suffix: "GPT-6 Astra (max)", "GPT-5.6 Luna (max)", "GPT-5.6 Terra (max)", "GPT-5.6 Sol (max)", "Claude Opus 5 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort)", "Claude Fable 5.1 (Adaptive Reasoning, Max Effort, Default Fallback)", "GPT-5.5 Pro (xhigh)". bench.match compares whole strings.

What (2 files: orchestrator/bench.py, tests/test_orchestrator.py; worktree off goal/T-0005 which contains B4a + T-0036):
1. bench.py: `def norm(name) -> str`: lowercase, strip everything from the first "(" to the matching ")", collapse whitespace, drop trailing punctuation. `match(records, hints)`: for each model id, candidates = records whose norm(name) == norm(hint) or norm(name).startswith(norm(hint) + " "); if several, prefer the one whose raw name contains "(max)" then "max effort" then "(xhigh)" then "(high)", else the first; record the chosen raw display name in the normalized record as "display_name" and all candidate raw names as "variants". Keep unmatched → None. Also: when a hint matches nothing, try a looser rule where the hint's tokens all appear in norm(name) (e.g. "gpt 5.6 luna" vs "gpt-5.6 luna" — normalize "-" to space on both sides).
2. tests: extend the fixture-based tests: names with suffixes match their ids; the "(max)" variant wins over "(high)" when both exist; "GPT-5.5 Pro (xhigh)" must NOT match a hint "GPT-5.5" unless such a hint exists (guard against prefix over-matching: startswith requires a space boundary and the remaining text must be only a parenthetical, i.e. compare norm strings for equality after stripping, and the token rule requires all hint tokens and no extra alphabetic tokens except effort words).
3. After the change run one live `uv run orchestrator bench fetch --force` and report matched/unmatched; expect ≥6 of 8 hints matched.

Run `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py`. Commit: "bench: match display names with effort suffixes; prefer the max variant" with a revert-path body.
acceptance: uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py exits 0 with the new matching tests
one live bench fetch --force matches at least 6 of the 8 DEFAULT_HINTS and bench show lists numbers for gpt-6-astra and gpt-5.6-luna/terra/sol
GPT-5.5 Pro does not match the gpt-6-astra or 5.6 hints (test)
git diff --stat limited to orchestrator/bench.py and tests/test_orchestrator.py

result.summary:
Committed clean. Working tree is clean now.

**Summary:** Added `norm()` (strips the first parenthetical, lowercases, collapses whitespace) and reworked `match()` in `orchestrator/bench.py` to compare normalized names, tolerate a trailing effort word outside parens, and fall back to dash/space-insensitive token matching — guarded against prefix over-matching. When multiple effort variants satisfy a hint, it now prefers `(max)` > `max effort` > `(xhigh)` > `(high)`, and records `display_name`/`variants` on the match.

**Files changed:** `orchestrator/bench.py`, `tests/test_orchestrator.py` (both in scope).

**Test output:** `uv run python -m unittest tests/test_orchestrator.py` — 59 tests, all pass, no failures. `scripts_green.sh` equivalent exited 0.

**Live verification:** `uv run orchestrator bench fetch --force` matched 6/8 `DEFAULT_HINTS` (unmatched: claude-haiku-4-5, claude-sonnet-5 — not currently listed under those names on the site). `bench show` confirms numbers for `gpt-6-astra`, `gpt-5.6-luna`, `gpt-5.6-terra`, `gpt-5.6-sol`.

Committed as `e29a97e` on `task/T-0037`.
